description: Create the backend FastAPI service in backend/, containerized with a python:3.12-slim + uvicorn Docker image. It exposes a public health endpoint for ALB health checks and a JWT-protected /hello endpoint returning 'Hello World'. JWTs are Cognito-issued and verified against the Cognito JWKS. The service reads config from the env vars defined in infra/compute.yaml (FEAT-001) and has IAM access to the content S3 bucket (a small helper to read from S3 demonstrates the wiring). Depends on FEAT-001 for exact env var names, container port 8000, and health path /health.
steps: Create backend/pyproject.toml (or requirements.txt) pinning: fastapi, uvicorn[standard], python-jose[cryptography] (or PyJWT[crypto]) for JWT verification, httpx (fetch JWKS), boto3 (S3), pydantic-settings, pytest, respx/pytest-httpx for tests.

backend/app/config.py: pydantic-settings Settings reading COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID, COGNITO_REGION (default us-east-1), COGNITO_CLIENT_ID, COGNITO_ISSUER (default built as https://cognito-idp.<region>.amazonaws.com/<pool_id>), AWS_REGION, CONTENT_BUCKET, PORT (default 8000). Names MUST match infra/compute.yaml env vars.

backend/app/auth.py: fetch and cache the Cognito JWKS from <issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json; a FastAPI dependency get_current_user that reads the Bearer token, verifies signature against JWKS (RS256), validates issuer and token_use ('access' or 'id') and expiry, and returns claims. On failure raise HTTP 401. Structure so the JWKS client is injectable/mocked in tests.
backend/app/s3.py: a small boto3 client wrapper with a function to list/get objects from CONTENT_BUCKET, demonstrating the task role S3 access (used by a future content API; keep minimal).

backend/app/main.py: FastAPI app. Public GET /health -> {'status':'ok'} (no auth) for the ALB target group. Protected GET /hello depending on get_current_user -> returns 'Hello World' (JSON like {'message':'Hello World'} or plain text 'Hello World'; keep the exact string 'Hello World'). Mount routes so that behind CloudFront '/api/*' the paths resolve (decide whether app serves /api/hello or /hello and document it; the ALB receives what CloudFront forwards — align with frontend FEAT-003 and infra path behavior). Include a root or docs route as convenient.

backend/Dockerfile: FROM python:3.12-slim, install deps, copy app, expose 8000, run `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`. Add a HEALTHCHECK hitting /health optionally. Add backend/.dockerignore.

backend/tests/: pytest tests. test_health: GET /health returns 200 without auth. test_hello_requires_auth: GET /hello without token -> 401. test_hello_with_valid_token: mock JWKS/verification so a valid token yields 200 and body contains 'Hello World'. test_hello_invalid_token -> 401. Use FastAPI TestClient and dependency_overrides or mocked JWKS.
backend/README.md: how to run locally (uvicorn), env vars, how to build/run the Docker image, and how the ALB health check and Cognito JWT verification work.
acceptance_criteria: GET /health returns HTTP 200 with no Authorization header (satisfies ALB health check).
GET the protected hello route without a valid Bearer token returns HTTP 401.
GET the protected hello route with a valid (mocked) Cognito token returns HTTP 200 and the response body contains the exact string 'Hello World'.
JWT verification validates the signature against the Cognito JWKS and checks issuer and expiry (not merely decoding without verification).
The container image builds with `docker build backend/` and starts uvicorn on port 8000.
Config env var names in backend match those declared in infra/compute.yaml exactly.
verification: Run backend tests with python 3.12: `pyenv local 3.12 || true` then create a venv, install deps, and run `pytest backend/tests -q`. Confirm all tests pass.
Run `docker build -t course-backend backend/` and confirm the image builds successfully.
Optionally run the container and curl http://localhost:8000/health expecting 200 and /hello without token expecting 401.
